subject: Post-demo SLO recap + customer-led load rehearsal — next steps
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@aerocorp.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 16:12:00 +0000
Subject: Post-demo SLO recap + customer-led load rehearsal — next steps

Hi Samir / Jules,

Thanks again for a productive demo earlier — appreciate the clarity on your customer-facing latency targets. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get the customer-led load rehearsal on the calendar.

Recap of SLOs you called out (from today's discovery):
- 95th percentile single-response latency <= 350ms for text-generation (payloads ~120 tokens).
- Sustained throughput target: 40 concurrent streaming connections or equivalent 1.2k requests/minute (bursty patterns ok, see below).
- Streaming tail latency (95p) target <= 500ms for multi-chunk responses.
- No output-quality regression vs baseline prompts (we'll run the eval set during dry run).

Proposed customer-led rehearsal plan:
1) Provide a test account + API key from Redwood (we can create a scoped key limited to the test environment).
2) Share our draft runbook & k6 scripts (attached). You map traffic to your locust scenarios or use our k6 repo.
3) IP allowlist: we will give the IP ranges used by our runners and the Dedicated nodes to add to your firewall for the test window.
4) Test window: please propose two 2-hour windows next week (PDT preferred). We recommend an initial dry run (ramp to 50% target) then full rehearsal.
5) On-call: Ethan (infra) will be on the call for infra-level metrics and can push tweaks (batching/kv cache warmup) if we see cold-start spikes.

Action items for AeroCorp:
- Confirm which test window(s) work and which traffic profile you want to run (steady vs burst).
- Confirm whether you'll run k6 or Locust so we can provide mapping notes.
- Provide a point of contact for network team (for allowlist coordination).

Next steps from our side:
- I'll provision a scoped test API key and share creds securely once you confirm the window.
- Ethan will post the IP ranges and the k6 example repo link in a follow-up email.
- We'll lock the runbook and mark the success criteria in the Drive folder.

Attached: Draft runbook (20260511_SLO_Runbook_DRAFT.pdf), sample k6 script (aerocorp_k6_script_v1.js).

If that looks good, propose the windows and we'll lock in resources.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0104

---

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@aerocorp.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jules Hamid <jules@aerocorp.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo SLO recap + customer-led load rehearsal — next steps

Thanks Stephanie — great summary. A couple of clarifications from our side before we confirm windows:

1) Latency/throughput: The 350ms 95p target is for single-turn chat completions that our UI stitches into a single response. For streaming paths we care more about time-to-first-chunk and then stable chunk throughput (we'll validate both).
2) Traffic profile: we'll test two profiles — (A) conversational steady state: 40 concurrent streaming sessions with intermittent user typing (bursty messages every 10–30s) and (B) synthetic spike: rapid-fire 2k req/min for 3 minutes to validate fallback behavior.
3) Network: our security team needs the exact IP ranges and the FQDNs that will be called from your runners (we cannot open broad CIDR ranges).

Windows: Thu 14 May 2026 16:00–18:00 PDT or Fri 15 May 2026 09:00–11:00 PDT; prefer the 14 May slot if Redwood can support a 30-minute preflight at 15:15 PDT.

Please send the IPs and provisional API key to Jules (jules@aerocorp.com) and our infra mailbox infra+tests@aerocorp.com. We'll get the firewall ticket opened immediately once we have those details.

Samir
Sr. Product Manager | AeroCorp
samir.patel@aerocorp.com

---

From: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@aerocorp.com>, Jules Hamid <jules@aerocorp.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 18:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-demo SLO recap + customer-led load rehearsal — next steps

Hey Samir / Jules — looping in infra details and concrete artifacts.

1) Test API key: We'll provision a scoped key limited to the staging model set and a fixed token quota. Expect a secure link (1-time download) from our secrets service shortly after you confirm the window.

2) IP/FQDN allowlist (runners + dedicated nodes):
- Runner NAT IPs (k6 cloud): 35.196.12.8, 35.196.12.9, 35.196.12.10
- Redwood Dedicated egress (us-west-2): 52.24.130.45, 52.24.130.46
- Hostnames our clients call (HTTPS): api.redwood-inference.com, staging.api.redwood-inference.com

We can provide a signed ASN/CIDR set if you prefer prefix ranges instead of single IPs. Note: if your firewall only allows FQDNs, the hostnames above resolve to dynamic IPs; we'll work with your network team to meet their standard.

3) k6/Locust mapping & repo:
- k6 examples: https://github.com/redwood-inference/k6-scripts/tree/aerocorp-v1 (includes steady-state and spike scenarios).
- Locust: we added a mapping guide in the repo (locust_mapping.md) — highlights: set streaming connection keepalive to true, set chunk size to match your UI, and warm KV cache with the first 5 minutes at 25% traffic.

4) Streaming guidance:
- Warm-up: 10–15 minute prefix warmup with low ramp to populate KV caches for embeddings and attention keys.
- Concurrency: we recommend limiting initial test to 60 concurrent streaming sessions for safety; we will then step down to your target 40 concurrent to validate latencies.
- Metrics we will watch: per-worker p95 latency, time-to-first-chunk, token/sec, system GPU utilization, and egress throughput.

5) Runbook & attachments: attached is the same draft runbook Stephanie shared. The aerocorp_k6_script_v1.js in the repo is what we recommend you run for the steady-state.

6) Preflight and on-call: We can do the 30-minute preflight at 15:15 PDT on Thu 14 May. I'll be on the preflight + main window along with a telemetry engineer. Ben will be on the call for any contract/SLA clarifications.

Let me know if you need the IPs as CIDR blocks or a signed document for your security ticket and we'll generate that.

Thanks,
Ethan Park
Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference
ethan_park@redwood.ai

Attachment stubs: aerocorp_k6_script_v1.js (script), 20260511_SLO_Runbook_DRAFT.pdf (runbook)

Perfect — the 14 May slot works and we'll plan the 30-minute preflight. I'll open the firewall ticket now and include the two runner IPs + dedicated egress IPs you listed. Jules will confirm whether we need CIDR blocks; if so we'll follow up by EOD.

We'll plan to run both profiles (steady-state then synthetic spike). Please send the secure key link when ready and post any final runbook edits to the Drive folder. We'll invite infra+tests and our security POC to the preflight.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — see you Thursday.

Samir
